title: Creek corridor planting
accessibilityNotes: A paved path leads to the meeting point. Planting takes place on uneven ground; a seated seedling-preparation activity is available.
description: Spend a morning helping native plants find a home along the creek corridor. Learn how small patches of vegetation create shelter for local birds and insects, then work together to plant and mulch seedlings.
bring: Closed shoes, a hat and a refillable water bottle. Tools and gloves are provided in this fictional activity.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Footscray suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.

title: A little native garden
accessibilityNotes: Step-free entry, wide paths and seated workstations. The workshop includes a quiet break area.
description: A balcony, courtyard or tiny backyard can make room for nature. Explore a selection of native plants, learn about sunlight and soil, and sketch a small garden that suits your space.
bring: A notebook and an idea of the sunlight in your space. Sample pots and materials are provided.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Brunswick suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.

title: Meet your local pollinators
accessibilityNotes: A slow, one-kilometre walk on a mostly level gravel path. Benches are available along the route.
description: Slow down and notice the small visitors keeping our gardens growing. Practise observing pollinators without disturbing them and discover simple ways to create habitat at home.
bring: Comfortable shoes and water. A camera or magnifying glass is optional.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Dandenong suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.

title: Give the woodland a hand
accessibilityNotes: Uneven ground and some bending and lifting. Rest breaks and shaded seating are available at the meeting point.
description: Help established seedlings through spring with careful weeding, watering and fresh mulch. This session suits volunteers with some previous outdoor conservation experience.
bring: Sturdy shoes, long trousers, sun protection and water. Hand tools are provided.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Sunshine suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.

title: Plant a pocket of green
accessibilityNotes: Step-free meeting area. Garden beds have mixed surfaces, with potting benches available for seated participation.
description: Join a small group to add layers of native greenery to a shared neighbourhood space. Learn where different plants belong and help prepare a welcoming patch for people and wildlife.
bring: Closed shoes, sun protection and water. Gloves, plants and tools are provided.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Preston suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.

title: Make room for wildlife
accessibilityNotes: Step-free classroom and accessible seating. The short outdoor demonstration can also be viewed from the paved terrace.
description: Explore how plants, leaf litter and water can create a more inviting garden for wildlife. Leave with a simple plan for one practical change to your own outdoor space.
bring: A notebook and a photo or sketch of your garden, if you have one.
mapLocationLabel: Approximate Richmond suburb reference point; not a confirmed meeting point.
